extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and applicants involved in USPTO prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling abstracts/abbreviatures/defensive publications, and detailed procedural rules for interviews (in-person, telephone, video, e-mail), recordation requirements, who may attend, timing, and limited rules on amendments and exhibits during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of express abandonment after issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An express abandonment arriving after the issue fee has been paid will not be accepted without a showing of one of the reasons indicated in 37 CFR 1.313(c), or else a showing under 37 CFR 1.183 justifying suspension of 37 CFR 1.313.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also MPEP § 711.01. An applicant must show one of the enumerated reasons or obtain relief under 1.183 for late express abandonment after payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts as publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts were prepared and published (per Notice of January 25, 1949) and each abstract includes a summary of the disclosure and, where drawings exist, a figure; publication of such abstracts was discontinued in 1953.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts are printed publications and are cited as prior art effective from the date of publication in the Official Gazette. Treat as publications for citation and prior-art purposes (see MPEP § 2136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviatures (per Notice of October 13, 1964) contain a specific portion of the disclosure, preferably a detailed representative claim and, if drawings exist, a figure; the publication of such abbreviatures was discontinued in 1965.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviatures are publications and should be cited accordingly as prior art; include citation format examples when listing in references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive Publication Program rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Defensive Publication Program (available April 1968–May 8, 1985) published abstracts of technical disclosure where applicant waived enforceable patent rights; publication provisionally abandoned the application but retained limited interference rights for 5 years from earliest U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defensive publication is prior art only as of its publication date (not an application publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)). Effect on benefit claiming: a continuing application must be filed within 30 months of the earliest effective U.S. filing date to claim the earlier date; limited rules allow certain later copending continuations if the first continuing application was timely filed. Distinct numbering schemes and citation/listing conventions apply; see conversion table references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and use of abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications as references
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications are to be referred to as publications and are cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) effective from the date of publication in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application (or portion) from which such a publication was prepared may itself be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) effective from actual U.S. filing date. These publications may be used alone or in combination with other prior art to reject claims under 102 and 103. Provide citations in specified formats (e.g., list abstracts/abbreviatures under 'Other References' and defensive publications with 'U.S. Patent Documents').

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The personal appearance of an applicant, attorney, or agent before the examiner or a telephone conversation or video conference or electronic mail between such parties presenting matters for the examiner’s consideration is considered an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition encompasses in-person, telephonic, video, and e-mail exchanges when substantive matters are presented; see 37 CFR 1.133.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location and hours for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours, as the respective examiners may designate; interviews will not be permitted at any other time or place without authority of the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible locations include examiner offices, conference rooms, and the Video Conference Center (VCC). Interviews are permissible on any working day except during periods of overtime work. Exceptions require Commissioner approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of interviews relative to first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview for the discussion of the patentability of a pending application will not occur before the first Office action, unless the application is a continuing or substitute application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for interviews prior to first Office action are ordinarily granted only in continuing or substitute applications; generally, requests before first action in other applications are untimely and will not be acknowledged or granted (37 CFR 1.133(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement required when reconsideration is requested after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview with an examiner, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions as specified in §§ 1.111 and 1.135. See 37 CFR 1.133(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and advance arrangement of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should normally be arranged in advance (by letter, fax, e-mail, telegram or telephone) to ensure primary examiner and/or examiner in charge will be present; a VCC interview must be arranged at least 3 days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a second art unit is involved, check availability of the second examiner. Keep appointments; notify other party promptly if circumstances change. Grouped interviews and arrangements for out-of-town attorneys are discussed; examiner may require scheduling in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate purposes and preparation for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be had only when the nature of the case is such that the interview could serve to develop and clarify specific issues and lead to a mutual understanding between the examiner and the applicant; the attorney when presenting for an interview should be fully prepared to discuss the issues raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should indicate in advance what issues are to be discussed, preferably by submitting a proposed amendment in writing to permit examiner preparation. Interviews may be refused if attorney is not prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable duration and avoiding interruptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties to the interview must see that it is not extended beyond a reasonable period, usually not longer than 30 minutes; the primary examiner must ensure the interview is not extended beyond a reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should avoid unnecessary interruptions during interviews; notify receptionist to not complete incoming calls unless emergency. Exceptions for interviews that require more time may be considered, but generally limit to a reasonable period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone call protocol for lengthy discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telephone call is made and it becomes evident that a lengthy discussion will ensue or the examiner needs time to restudy, the call should be terminated with agreement that the examiner will call back at a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls originated by the examiner should be made through the Federal Telecommunications System (FTS) even if a collect call is authorized. Include complete telephone number (area code and extension) in correspondence and transmittals to facilitate callbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview substance must be made of record (use PTOL-413)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any face-to-face, video conference, electronic mail or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement was reached at the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.133(b) and MPEP § 502.03. The Interview Summary form PTOL-413 shall be given a paper number, placed in the file, and listed on the file wrapper contents. Duplicate copy given to applicant at conclusion (or mailed/faxed for non-personal interviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Items required on Interview Summary (PTOL-413)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTOL-413 form provides for recordation of: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date of interview; (E) type of interview; (F) name of participants; (G) indication whether an exhibit was shown; (H) identification of claims discussed; (I) identification of specific prior art discussed; (J) indication whether an agreement was reached and description; (K) signature of examiner; (L) names of other USPTO personnel present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form reminds the applicant of responsibility to record substance of interview. When the substance is adequately recorded on PTOL-413 or attachment, examiner may check box indicating applicant need not supplement form. An examiner’s amendment that incorporates the complete recordation may substitute for completing PTOL-413.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required substantive content when recording interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete and proper recordation of the substance of any interview should include at least applicable items: (A) brief description of any exhibit shown or demonstration; (B) identification of claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed substantive amendments discussed; (E) general thrust of principal arguments of applicant and examiner; (G) general results or outcome of the interview; (H) for electronic mail interviews, a paper copy of the Internet e-mail contents must be placed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of arguments need not be verbatim or highly detailed; general nature sufficient so principal arguments are understood in context. Examiner expected to carefully review applicant’s record of interview; may give applicant one month under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to supply omissions or corrections for replies to nonfinal Office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and marking of interview record accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s summary of the interview should be carefully checked for accuracy; if the record is complete and accurate, the examiner should place the indication 'Interview record OK' on the paper recording and date and initial it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is an inaccuracy that bears directly on patentability, the examiner should point it out in the next Office letter. If claims are allowable for other reasons, the examiner should send letter setting forth his/her version of the statement attributed to him/her.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be granted interviews / authority requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not generally granted to persons who lack proper authority from the applicant or attorney/agent of record in the form of a paper on file in the application or do not have possession of a copy of the application file; a mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority for interviews involving merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered local representatives known to represent the attorney may be granted interviews even if power of attorney not of record; for telephone interviews by a registered practitioner not of record, faxing a power of attorney before the interview is recommended. Interviews normally not granted unless requesting party has authority to bind the principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection is permitted, but the intended purpose and content should be presented briefly (preferably in writing) in advance; interviews merely to restate arguments of record or to discuss new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration should be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A second or further interview after final rejection may be held if examiner is convinced it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal. Interviews may be held after expiration of the shortened statutory period and prior to the maximum permitted statutory period without an extension of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discussing inter partes questions ex parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes substantive matters must be handled in the appropriate inter partes procedures; ex parte interviews cannot be used to explore inter partes issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure of other cases during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview in the examiner’s room, the examiner should arrange his or her desk so that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary in the interview, are placed out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality of other applicants' files and comply with MPEP § 101; avoid inadvertent exposure of unrelated materials during interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations, exhibits, and models rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention may be exhibited or demonstrated during the interview by a model. A model received by the examiner which complies with 37 CFR 1.91 and which is made part of the application record must be properly recorded on the 'Contents' portion of the application file wrapper. If a model/exhibit is merely used for demonstration and not made part of the record, a full description of what was demonstrated/exhibited must be made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrations of apparatus too large to be brought into the Office may be viewed outside the Office with supervisory approval. Attorneys wishing to show videotapes must demonstrate relevance and obtain prior supervisory approval; VCC scheduling and recording rules apply. Where demonstration is essential to developing/clarifying issues, allow viewing with appropriate approvals and recordation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after notice of allowance / during issue process
rubrics_metrics.description: After an application is sent to issue (technical jurisdiction change under 37 CFR 1.312), an interview involving detailed consideration of claims or prior art to determine allowability should not be given; requests for interviews on cases where a notice of allowance has been mailed should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a showing in writing of extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant is not entitled to a greater degree of consideration informally than is provided by formal amendments; consideration of an amendment presented informally after issue may not be demanded as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making amendments in application (37 CFR 1.121) — specification other than claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the specification (other than claims and certain listings) are made by submitting: (i) an instruction unambiguously identifying the location to delete, replace, or add a paragraph; (ii) any replacement or added paragraph(s) in clean form (without markings); and (iii) another version of any replacement paragraph(s) on pages separate from the amendment, marked up to show all changes relative to the previous version (brackets for deletions, underlining for additions, or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A marked-up version is not required for purely added or deleted paragraphs beyond stating that a paragraph has been added or deleted. Amendments must comply with § 1.52 and filing requirements. This provides for clear identification of changes and facilitates examiner processing.
